replication.target_description: Study 1, non-direct replication in French-speaking computer users: confirmatory omnibus three-condition ANOVA of absolute moral-judgment deviation from midpoint 4; no age/gender covariates.

notes:
Both primary full papers were retrieved and their titles/DOIs verified. Original target is the omnibus effect on judgment polarization (partial eta-squared .07), rather than its separate pairwise contrasts. Replication uses the matching Study 1 confirmatory omnibus analysis; it is explicitly described by its authors as a non-direct replication owing to French-language materials and preceding questionnaire battery. Printed replication partial eta-squared is an upper bound, retained verbatim. Original n is reported in Method and supported by the ANOVA degrees of freedom; no exclusions are documented. HAL adds a cover page, so article page numbers differ from PDF positions by one for the replication.
Completion source review (n_r): Explicit final computer-user sample of 8602 in Study 1, linked to its unadjusted confirmatory three-background model. Recruitment and exploratory samples are distinct; no df inference or N summation.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Page-4 Study 1 confirmatory omnibus result prints partial eta-squared < 0.001 with F(2, 8599) = 2.72. Retained printed inequality and metric; not a conversion from contrast d.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Exact printed p=.06 belongs to the same page-4 unadjusted omnibus test as the extracted partial eta-squared.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors explicitly state inability to observe black-and-white priming polarizing moral judgment in Study 1; failed is their narrative verdict. The non-direct design and procedural limitations are recorded in notes.
